status_note: active, but this repo is only the client SDKs (packages/core, packages/react gen1, packages/sdks gen2 generated by Mitosis for React/Vue/Svelte/Solid/Qwik/Angular/React-Native), examples, starters and editor plugins. The visual editor, content API/CDN, Figma import and 'Visual Copilot' AI are closed SaaS at builder.io; the editor cannot be self-hosted.
core_problem: A headless visual CMS: marketers assemble pages in a SaaS editor from registered code components plus free-form styled boxes, and the resulting JSON is fetched and rendered by an SDK in the host app's framework.
architecture: Content model (packages/core/src/types/content.ts, element.ts): BuilderContent { id, name, published: 'published'|'draft'|'archived', modelId, '@version', data: { blocks: BuilderElement[], inputs, state, ... }, variations: { [id]: { data, name, testRatio } }, startDate/endDate }. BuilderElement { '@type': '@builder.io/sdk:Element', '@version', id, tagName, layerName, children: BuilderElement[], responsiveStyles: { large|medium|small|xsmall: Partial<CSSStyleDeclaration> }, component?: { name, options }, bindings: { [path]: jsExpressionString }, properties (HTML attrs), actions: { [event]: jsString }, code: { bindings, actions } (user-authored source that transpiles into bindings), repeat: { collection, itemName }, animations, meta, groupLocked/layerLocked }. Every element is a styled DOM box; a component is an optional annotation on the box, and dynamic behaviour is string JS evaluated at render (packages/react/src/functions/string-to-function.ts; isolated-vm on the server for gen2 SDKs). Registration (packages/core/src/builder.class.ts): Builder.registerComponent(Component, { name, inputs: Input[], defaultStyles, canHaveChildren, noWrap, defaultChildren, defaults, childRequirements: { message, component | query (sift.js Mongo-style) }, requiresParent: { message, component | query }, models, group, hideFromInsertMenu, requiredPermissions, isRSC, meta }). Input { name, type: string (open string: 'text','longText','richText','number','boolean','color','file','object','list','reference','code'...), required, defaultValue, enum, regex: { pattern, options, message }, subFields, showIf (fn|string), localized, advanced, broadcast, bubble, helperText, model, meta }. Registration side-effect: window.parent.postMessage({ type: 'builder.registerComponent', data: spec }) so the SaaS editor learns the catalogue from the running page. Visual editing: the host page is loaded in an iframe inside builder.io; packages/react/src/scripts/init-editing.ts announces { type: 'builder.isReactSdk', supportsPatchUpdates: 'v4', supportsCustomBreakpoints, supportsGlobalSymbols, blockLevelPersonalization } as a capability handshake; the editor pushes 'builder.updateContent' / JSON patches that BuilderBlock applies with apply-patch-with-mutation.ts; each block renders with class 'builder-block' and builder-id attributes, responsiveStyles compiled to emotion CSS with max-width media queries (builder-block.component.tsx emotionCss). Rendering: <BuilderComponent model=... content=...> -> BuilderBlocks -> BuilderBlock (class component) -> registered component or raw tag; gen2 SDKs reimplement the same in Mitosis .lite.tsx blocks (packages/sdks/src/blocks/*) with component-info.ts descriptors. Undo/redo, versioning, scheduling, A/B, personalization live server-side in the SaaS.
core_innovation: Compile one editor-agnostic block JSON (styled boxes + component annotations + string bindings) to many frameworks via Mitosis, and let the running page register its own component catalogue into the editor through postMessage.
strengths: Declarative structural constraints on the catalogue: childRequirements and requiresParent accept either a component name or a sift.js query over the element JSON, with a human-readable violation message.
Capability negotiation between page SDK and editor (init-editing.ts flags) so the editor can degrade features per SDK version — a clean pattern for editor/preview version skew.
Content-level A/B variations with testRatio, schedules (startDate/endDate) and published state are first-class on the document, not bolted on.
Every element is self-describing ('@type', '@version'), which makes the JSON safe to migrate and to validate per node.
Input schema has practical validation affordances (regex with message, enum, required, showIf, localized) and 'reference' inputs to other content models.
Multi-framework output from one source (Mitosis) proves a block model can stay framework-neutral if the renderer is a pure function of JSON.
weaknesses: The core unit is a free-form styled box with per-breakpoint arbitrary CSS in the content JSON — exactly the 'Hero 1/2/3 with free styling' model we rejected; design quality is left to the marketer.

Dynamic behaviour is string-evaluated JavaScript (stringToFunction / new Function / isolated-vm) inside content — a security surface and a runtime-JS requirement that conflicts with a near-zero-JS Astro output.
The editor, content API, CDN, versioning, undo/redo and AI are closed SaaS; the repo gives no editor to adapt and no DOM->data mapping code beyond builder-id attributes.
No Astro SDK; gen1 React SDK is class components + emotion; gen2 SDKs still need a client runtime for bindings, state and personalization.
Input.type is an open string, Component.inputs are runtime arrays, not a discriminated union or Zod schema — weak compile-time typing of the catalogue.
Repo is a 340 MB monorepo with generated SDK outputs checked in; heavy to read and irrelevant to our stack.
Content model mixes concerns (layout, styling, data binding, behaviour, personalization) in one element type, so no gate can reason about layout separately from copy.
patterns_to_steal: childRequirements/requiresParent with a query predicate + message -> Compat filter / section library: declare parent/child compatibility as data (e.g. testimonial_grid requires_parent: proof_first archetype beats) and reuse the message in the Gap Report.

SDK<->editor capability handshake -> visual_editor: when the Astro preview iframe boots, it should announce which edit affordances it supports (inline text, image swap, section reorder) so the editor UI enables only those.
Per-node '@type'/'@version' tags -> SiteDefinition: version each section node so migrations and validators can target individual node kinds.
Document-level variations { testRatio } + schedule -> telemetry/priors: keep the shape in mind for future variant experiments over arrangements, computed server-side, never in client JS.
Input.regex { pattern, message } and localized flags -> Zod field schemas for owner-editable copy (length/regex bounds with human messages surfaced in the editor).
patterns_to_avoid: responsiveStyles per element in content JSON -> design tokens must come from the selected design_system_id; styles never live in the document.
String JS bindings/actions evaluated at render -> violates JS budget and determinism; all data binding happens at build time from FactRegistry.

Registering the catalogue from the running page via postMessage -> our catalogue is a versioned, human-reviewed artefact; the editor must load it from the same Zod source as the renderer, not discover it from a live page.
Depending on a SaaS editor for the owner-facing surface -> the post-V1 editor must be self-hosted over our own SiteDefinition.
reusable_patterns: StructuralPredicateConstraint: a component declares requiresParent/childRequirements as a data query plus a user-facing message; the editor and validators both enforce it.
CapabilityHandshake: the embedded preview announces a feature-flag object on boot so the host editor enables only supported affordances.
TaggedVersionedNode: each node carries '@type' and '@version' so per-node migration and validation are possible.
VariationEnvelope: a document carries named variations with ratios and schedules alongside the default payload.
BindingIndirection: dynamic values are stored as expressions in a separate 'bindings' map keyed by target path rather than inline in props (pattern only; we would bind to FactRegistry ids, not JS).
adoption_strategy: Ignore — The open-source part is only delivery SDKs for a closed editor, and the content model (free-form responsive CSS per box + string-evaluated JS bindings) is the antithesis of a constrained, token-driven, near-zero-JS site. Nothing here renders to Astro. Lift two small ideas into our own schemas: the requiresParent/childRequirements predicate-with-message shape for section compatibility, and the preview capability handshake for the post-V1 editor. Do not spend further time on the monorepo.
